name: What are the differences between an attached and a detached ADU?

mainEntity.name: What are the differences between an attached and a detached ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached ADU shares a wall with the primary residence, often built as an extension or by converting existing space, while a detached ADU is a standalone structure on the property. Attached ADUs may be more cost-effective due to shared utility connections and foundation work, but detached ADUs offer greater privacy and design flexibility. Your choice between an attached or detached unit often depends on available backyard space, budget, and desired level of separation from the main home.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attached ADUs share a wall with the main house; detached ADUs are separate structures. Attached may be cheaper, detached offers more privacy.
